```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Workflow requirements {#workflow-requirements}

Use a genetic reference panel matched to the GWAS ancestry and genome build.
The default database uses GRCh37. Convert coordinates from other builds and
check marker identity and allele orientation before ingestion. Required fields
are `chr`, `pos`, `ea`, `nea`, `b`, `seb`, and `p`. Supply study effect-allele
frequencies as `eaf` when available. When `eaf` is omitted, gact uses the marker
catalog frequencies, so the study-to-reference frequency check needs study EAF.

Review the mappings returned by `detectStatSchema()` when using automatic
mapping. Use `effect_scale = "beta"` for a beta or log-odds column and
`effect_scale = "or"` for odds ratios from a column with a different name.
By default, `ingestStatDB()` converts columns named `OR` or `odds_ratio` to
log odds. Supply `seb` on the same scale as the resulting effect estimate.

Beta values must be finite, standard errors must be finite and positive, and
reported EAF must be between 0 and 1. By default, gact converts named
`-log10(p)` columns such as `neglog10p` and `LP`. Use
`p_scale = "neglog10p"` for other negative log10 p-value columns, or
`p_scale = "p"` for ordinary p-values.


## UK Biobank HbA1c example

Use `Glycated_haemoglobin_HbA1c.imp.gz` from version 1 of the NIH Figshare
release (`10.35092/yhjc.12355382.v1`, file ID `22770197`). The release uses
GRCh37 and reports beta relative to `ALT`. [Release record](https://doi.org/10.35092/yhjc.12355382.v1) ·
[Exact imputed HbA1c file](https://nih.figshare.com/ndownloader/files/22770197)

The GWAS meta-analysis combines White British, non-British White, African,
and South Asian participants. The GWAS Catalog reports a **study-level
discovery sample size of 338,919** (327,177 European, 4,847 African, and
6,895 South Asian participants). [GWAS Catalog study GCST90019509](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/studies/GCST90019509)

The release does not report variant-level sample sizes. Record the study
total in `comments` and omit `n`, because gact would otherwise copy the
supplied count to every variant when the input has no `n` column.

<br>

```{r all-code, include=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(gact)
library(data.table)


# Load GAlist with information on gact database
GAlist <- readRDS(file="C:/Users/gact/hsa.0.0.1/GAlist_hsa.0.0.1.rds")


# Load the imputed HbA1c file from the Figshare release cited above.
fname_stat <- "C:/Users/gact/hsa.0.0.1/download/Glycated_haemoglobin_HbA1c.imp.gz"
stat <- fread(fname_stat, data.table = FALSE)

# Map the study columns. This example uses catalog frequencies for EAF.
schema <- c(chr = "#CHROM", pos = "POS", ea = "ALT", nea = "REF",
            b = "Effect", seb = "StdErr", p = "P-value")

result <- ingestStatDB(
  GAlist, stat, schema = schema, effect_scale = "beta", p_scale = "p",
  source = "NIH Figshare file 22770197 (Glycated_haemoglobin_HbA1c.imp.gz)",
  trait = "HbA1c", type = "quantitative", gender = "both", ancestry = "Mixed",
  build = "GRCh37", reference = "PMID:33462484",
  comments = "Study-level discovery sample size: 338,919 (GCST90019509)"
)
GAlist <- result$GAlist

# Save updated database
saveRDS(GAlist, file="C:/Users/gact/hsa.0.0.1/GAlist_hsa.0.0.1.rds", compress = FALSE)


```
